Here's your proposal. Quick note first: your Mnemon graph is currently small — **23 live insights, 308 edges**. So this is entirely feasible and will look clean, not a hairball.

## What the data looks like (verified from the DB)

Two tables power the whole thing:

- **insights** — one memory node. Fields worth visualizing: `category` (context/decision/fact/insight/general), `importance` (1–5), `effective_importance` (0–1, boosted by use), `tags`, `entities`, `created_at`.
- **edges** — directed links between insights, typed:
  - `temporal` (born around the same time)
  - `semantic` (similar content)
  - `causal` (one drove another)
  - `entity` (share a named entity, e.g. `start-hermes.sh`)

Bonus: Mnemon ships a built-in `mnemon viz --format html` that already emits a vis.js page. So we're not building from scratch — the question is whether to **use it as-is, or build a richer custom one**.

## Option A — Use the built-in `mnemon viz` (fastest, ~1 command)

`mnemon viz --format html -o graph.html` → drops a self-contained vis.js HTML file.

- Pros: zero code, includes node/edge data + physics layout out of the box.
- Cons: vanillas (default vis controls, no category coloring by default, no importance sizing by default). You get a graph, but it won't tell your story on its own.

## Option B — Custom single-file HTML app (my recommendation)

One hand-written `graph.html` (+, Three.js) fed by a tiny export step. This is the "very nice 3D visualization" version.

**Export step:** I'd query the DB directly (it's plain SQLite — schema confirmed above) and emit a JSON of `{nodes, edges}`. ~15 lines of Python. No extra daemon needed.

**Visualization (tools choice):**
- **3D XR** — `vis-network` is 2D; the built-in is 2D. For actual **3D** the clean options are **Three.js + ForceGraph3D** (react-force-graph-style), which gives the classic spinning 3D knowledge-graph sphere, or **Cytoscape.js** (2D, lightweight), or **G6**. I'd pick **Three.js/3d-force-graph** — it's exactly built for this and needs no build step if I self-host one file.

**How I'd enrich it so it actually narrates your memory:**
- **Node size** → `effective_importance` (bigger = more important/more recalled)
- **Node color** → `category` (decision/context/fact/insight/general, with legend)
- **Node label** → shorttext + category; title tooltip shows full memory + tags + created date
- **Edge color + thickness** → `edge_type` + `weight`
- **Toggle panel**: show/hide by category, filter by entity, slider for importance threshold
- **3D controls**: orbit/zoom, node dragging, auto-spin toggle
- Dark theme, self-contained (single HTML — open with a double-click, no server needed)

## Recommendation

Go **Option B** — it's one self-contained HTML file over a ~15-line SQLite export, and it turns your graph from "nodes and lines" into something you can actually *read* (importance, categories, clusters around `start-hermes.sh`, `CI`, `symlink`, etc.). Built-in `viz` is the fallback if you want the quick 2-second version first.

Deliverable: one HTML file (standalone), plus the tiny Python exporter, so you can re-generate any time your graph grows.

Two questions before I build:

1. **2D or true 3D?** The built-in is 2D. You said "3DJS" — do you want the full Three.js rotating-3D graph, or a refined 2D interactive one?
2. **Where should it live?** In the repo (so it's versioned and CI-friendly) or just scratch in `~/`?

Once you confirm, I'll build and open it for you.

**mnemon-graph.html** — the 3D knowledge-graph viewer for your Mnemon memory. Here's the full picture:

**What it is**
- A single self-contained 1.3 MB HTML file — the **built artifact** of the viewer
- Title: "Mnemon Knowledge Graph"

```
export_graph.py  ->  graph.json + graph-data.js   (your data, refreshed per export)
build.py         ->  mnemon-graph.html            (the viewer, only rebuilt when template.html changes)
template.html    ->  editable source that build.py uses
index.html       ->  tiny forwarder so http://host:8123/ lands on the viewer
```

- It does NOT embed the data — it loads `graph.json` (http) or `graph-data.js` (file:// double-click) at runtime, so refreshing data never requires rebuilding it
- Works both ways: `http://localhost:8123/mnemon-graph.html` or double-click the file directly

**mnemon-viz.html** — the 2D vis.js fallback, generated by Mnemon's own tool (not my custom build). Here's the distinction:

**What it is**
- **629 KB** self-contained HTML, generated by `mnemon viz --format html -o mnemon-viz.html`
- Uses **vis.js** (a 2D network graph library) — different rendering engine than the 3D one

```
                  mnemon-graph.html          mnemon-viz.html
----------------  -------------------------  -------------------------------
Engine            Three.js / 3d-force-graph  vis.js (2D)
Dimensionality    3D, auto-rotating          2D, flat network
Data              loads graph.json at runtime  embeds nodes+edges inline
Generated by      build.py (custom template)  mnemon viz (Mnemon's own tool)
Role              the pretty custom viewer    the "safe" fallback renderer
```

nodes.content:
Here's the proposal, grounded in the current code and measurements.

**What's actually happening**

- `frameGraph()` (runs when the sim settles) frames the graph so its bounding box fills **~72% of the view height** — on your 577px-tall viewport that puts the 145-node graph at ~490px tall, i.e. nearly the whole screen.
- The pills are **fixed-size DOM labels** (12px font, ~50–150px wide) that do NOT scale with zoom. With average node spacing around 30–35px, every pill overlaps its neighbors on the default view → it reads as "everything is too big / too zoomed in".
- There are **no zoom clamps** — wheel-scrolling can dive into a single pill wall or fly out into empty space.

**Options**

**Option A — Zoom out the default framing (recommended, 1-line change + pill tweak)**
Change the framing fill factor 0.72 → ~0.45, so the graph occupies roughly half the viewport height instead of nearly all of it. Pair with a modest pill shrink (12px → 10px font, tighter padding → pills ~30% narrower). Result: whole graph visible with breathing room, overlaps drop sharply, structure readable at a glance.
- Risk: near-zero. One constant + one CSS tweak. Fully verifiable in-browser.
- Tradeoff: the graph is smaller on screen — that's the point, but if you want details you zoom in.

**Option B — Zoom clamps (cheap hygiene, pairs with A)**
Set OrbitControls `minDistance`/`maxDistance` once in `frameGraph` (e.g. 0.35× and 4× the framing distance). Wheel-zoom can no longer slam into a pill or lose the graph entirely. ~4 lines.

**Option C — Auto-scale pills with zoom (the "proper" long-term fix, more work)**
In the per-frame label loop, scale pill size inversely with camera distance: zoom out → pills shrink (down to a floor, or fade to plain dots below a threshold); zoom in → pills grow. This keeps labels proportional to the graph at every zoom level, like map labels. Cost: per-frame style updates on 145 elements (transform-based, no reflow, but it's real DOM churn), plus a hide-below-threshold rule so distant pills don't become unreadable specks. Medium complexity, medium risk.

**My recommendation: A + B now.** It directly answers "zoom is too big" with a safer, verifiable change, and it's reversible in one commit. C is a nice follow-up if A+B still feels crowded after you've lived with it.

One check before you decide: by "zoom too big", do you mean the **default view is too close/crowded** (my read — A fixes this), or that **wheel-scrolling zooms too aggressively** (that's a different knob — OrbitControls `zoomSpeed`, ~2 lines)? Tell me which and which option(s) you want and I'll implement.
